-- ref SecondsToTime (UIParent.lua:1004-1031) and its GlobalStrings, in the ref's own home -- file — two consumers now (the quest-timer window and the quest log's "Time Remaining:" -- row, decision 1150), so it lives here rather than being redefined per file the way -- BuffFrame.xml had to for SecondsToTimeAbbrev when it was the only caller. -- -- Departures, both named: -- - `GetText(TOKEN, nil, n)` is the ref's plural-aware GlobalString lookup, a C binding we -- don't ship. Its enUS rule is the singular token for exactly 1 and the `_P1` twin -- otherwise — the same rule already codified in `tooltip_item/render.rs` and MailFrame.xml -- — so it collapses to the local `plural()` below and the four shipped string pairs -- (GlobalStrings.lua:895-896, 2296-2297, 2693-2694, 3404-3405). -- - Lua 5.1 dialect: `math.mod`/`math.floor` for the 5.0 bare `mod`/`floor`. -- -- Everything else is verbatim, INCLUDING the two behaviours that look like bugs and are -- not: the thresholds are strict `>` (86400 s reads as hours, not "1 Day"), and `count < 2` -- stops after two units, so a 3-day quest reads "3 Days 4 Hrs" and never mentions minutes. DAYS_ABBR = DAYS_ABBR or "Day" DAYS_ABBR_P1 = DAYS_ABBR_P1 or "Days" HOURS_ABBR = HOURS_ABBR or "Hr" HOURS_ABBR_P1 = HOURS_ABBR_P1 or "Hrs" MINUTES_ABBR = MINUTES_ABBR or "Min" MINUTES_ABBR_P1 = MINUTES_ABBR_P1 or "Mins" SECONDS_ABBR = SECONDS_ABBR or "Sec" SECONDS_ABBR_P1 = SECONDS_ABBR_P1 or "Secs"
if not SecondsToTime then local function plural(singular, pluralForm, n) if n == 1 then return singular end return pluralForm end
function SecondsToTime(seconds, noSeconds) local time = "" local count = 0 local tempTime seconds = math.floor(seconds) if seconds > 86400 then tempTime = math.floor(seconds / 86400) time = tempTime .. " " .. plural(DAYS_ABBR, DAYS_ABBR_P1, tempTime) .. " " seconds = math.mod(seconds, 86400) count = count + 1 end if seconds > 3600 then tempTime = math.floor(seconds / 3600) time = time .. tempTime .. " " .. plural(HOURS_ABBR, HOURS_ABBR_P1, tempTime) .. " " seconds = math.mod(seconds, 3600) count = count + 1 end if count < 2 and seconds >= 60 then tempTime = math.floor(seconds / 60) time = time .. tempTime .. " " .. plural(MINUTES_ABBR, MINUTES_ABBR_P1, tempTime) .. " " seconds = math.mod(seconds, 60) count = count + 1 end if count < 2 and seconds > 0 and not noSeconds then time = time .. seconds .. " " .. plural(SECONDS_ABBR, SECONDS_ABBR_P1, seconds) .. " " end return time end end
UIPARENT_MANAGED_FRAME_POSITIONS = {} -- Frames UIPARENT_MANAGED_FRAME_POSITIONS["MultiBarBottomLeft"] = {baseY = 17, reputation = 9, maxLevel = -5, anchorTo = "ActionButton1", point = "BOTTOMLEFT", rpoint = "TOPLEFT"} UIPARENT_MANAGED_FRAME_POSITIONS["GroupLootFrame1"] = {baseY = 60, bottomEither = 42, pet = 42, reputation = 9} UIPARENT_MANAGED_FRAME_POSITIONS["TutorialFrameParent"] = {baseY = 55, bottomEither = 47, pet = 42, reputation = 9} UIPARENT_MANAGED_FRAME_POSITIONS["FramerateLabel"] = {baseY = 64, bottomEither = 42, pet = 42, reputation = 9} UIPARENT_MANAGED_FRAME_POSITIONS["CastingBarFrame"] = {baseY = 60, bottomEither = 40, pet = 40, reputation = 9} UIPARENT_MANAGED_FRAME_POSITIONS["ChatFrame1"] = {baseY = 85, bottomLeft = 17, pet = 17, reputation = 9, maxLevel = -5, anchorTo = "UIParent", point = "BOTTOMLEFT", rpoint = "BOTTOMLEFT", xOffset = 32} UIPARENT_MANAGED_FRAME_POSITIONS["ChatFrame2"] = {baseY = 85, bottomRight = 17, rightLeft = -88, rightRight = -43, reputation = 9, maxLevel = -5, anchorTo = "UIParent", point = "BOTTOMRIGHT", rpoint = "BOTTOMRIGHT", xOffset = -32} UIPARENT_MANAGED_FRAME_POSITIONS["ShapeshiftBarFrame"] = {baseY = 0, bottomLeft = 45, reputation = 9, maxLevel = -5, anchorTo = "MainMenuBar", point = "BOTTOMLEFT", rpoint = "TOPLEFT", xOffset = 30}
-- Vars UIPARENT_MANAGED_FRAME_POSITIONS["CONTAINER_OFFSET_X"] = {baseX = 0, rightLeft = 90, rightRight = 45, isVar = "xAxis"} UIPARENT_MANAGED_FRAME_POSITIONS["CONTAINER_OFFSET_Y"] = {baseY = 70, bottomEither = 27, bottomRight = 0, reputation = 9, isVar = "yAxis", pet = 23} UIPARENT_MANAGED_FRAME_POSITIONS["BATTLEFIELD_TAB_OFFSET_Y"] = {baseY = 210, bottomRight = 40, reputation = 9, isVar = "yAxis"} UIPARENT_MANAGED_FRAME_POSITIONS["PETACTIONBAR_YPOS"] = {baseY = 97, bottomLeft = 43, reputation = 9, maxLevel = -5, isVar = "yAxis"}
function UIParent_ManageFramePositions() -- Frames that affect offsets in y axis local yOffsetFrames = {} -- Frames that affect offsets in x axis local xOffsetFrames = {}
-- Set up flags. Departure: the bottom flags read the always-on bars' visibility, -- not the ref's SHOW_MULTI_ACTIONBAR_1/2 option globals (0270 ships no such state). local bottomLeftShown = BenillaMultiBarBottomLeft and BenillaMultiBarBottomLeft:IsShown() local bottomRightShown = BenillaMultiBarBottomRight and BenillaMultiBarBottomRight:IsShown() if ( bottomLeftShown or bottomRightShown ) then table.insert(yOffsetFrames, "bottomEither") end if ( bottomRightShown ) then table.insert(yOffsetFrames, "bottomRight") end if ( bottomLeftShown ) then table.insert(yOffsetFrames, "bottomLeft") end
if ( MultiBarLeft and MultiBarLeft:IsShown() ) then table.insert(xOffsetFrames, "rightLeft") elseif ( MultiBarRight and MultiBarRight:IsShown() ) then table.insert(xOffsetFrames, "rightRight") end
if ( ( BenillaPetActionBarFrame and BenillaPetActionBarFrame:IsShown() ) or ( BenillaShapeshiftBarFrame and BenillaShapeshiftBarFrame:IsShown() ) ) then table.insert(yOffsetFrames, "pet") end if ( ReputationWatchBar and MainMenuExpBar and ReputationWatchBar:IsShown() and MainMenuExpBar:IsShown() ) then table.insert(yOffsetFrames, "reputation") end if ( MainMenuBarMaxLevelBar and MainMenuBarMaxLevelBar:IsShown() ) then table.insert(yOffsetFrames, "maxLevel") end
-- Iterate through frames and set anchors according to the flags set local frame, xOffset, yOffset, anchorTo, point, rpoint for index, value in pairs(UIPARENT_MANAGED_FRAME_POSITIONS) do frame = getglobal(index) if ( frame ) then -- Always start with base as the base offset or default to zero if no "none" specified xOffset = 0 if ( value["baseX"] ) then xOffset = value["baseX"] elseif ( value["xOffset"] ) then xOffset = value["xOffset"] end yOffset = 0 if ( value["baseY"] ) then yOffset = value["baseY"] end
-- Iterate through frames that affect y offsets local hasBottomLeft, hasPetBar, hasBottomRight for flag, flagValue in pairs(yOffsetFrames) do if ( value[flagValue] ) then if ( flagValue == "bottomLeft" ) then hasBottomLeft = 1 elseif ( flagValue == "pet" ) then hasPetBar = 1 elseif ( flagValue == "bottomRight" ) then hasBottomRight = 1 end yOffset = yOffset + value[flagValue] end end
if ( hasBottomLeft and hasPetBar ) then yOffset = yOffset + 23 end
-- Iterate through frames that affect x offsets for flag, flagValue in pairs(xOffsetFrames) do if ( value[flagValue] ) then xOffset = xOffset + value[flagValue] end end
-- Set up anchoring info anchorTo = value["anchorTo"] point = value["point"] rpoint = value["rpoint"] if ( not anchorTo ) then anchorTo = "UIParent" end if ( not point ) then point = "BOTTOM" end if ( not rpoint ) then rpoint = "BOTTOM" end
-- Anchor frame if ( value["isVar"] ) then if ( value["isVar"] == "xAxis" ) then _G[index] = xOffset else _G[index] = yOffset end else frame:SetPoint(point, anchorTo, rpoint, xOffset, yOffset) end end end
-- Custom positioning the row table cannot express (ref l.1705-1738). Both rules -- belong to the pet/stance ROW — the one row two different bars share — and without -- them the pet bar lands on top of the bottom-left multibar's buttons -- (director-caught: the bar drew across a row of spells, border and all). -- -- (a) The shelf art IS the pet bar's border, and it only makes sense when the bar -- sits directly on the main bar. Raised a row it would draw across whatever is -- underneath, so the ref hides both strips (l.1707-1708) — the same move it makes -- for the stance bar's own end-caps, which is why benilla's stance bar has none -- (0270 anchors it statically at the raised position). -- (b) The pet bar is the only managed entry whose row is a VAR: the loop above writes -- the NUMBER PETACTIONBAR_YPOS (97, +43 with the bottom-left bar up) and anchors -- nothing, so the ref re-seats the frame with it here (l.1735-1736). -- -- Departure: the ref computes PETACTIONBAR_XPOS in ShowPetActionBar() and reads it -- here, which only works because its bar slides in over several frames. Ours appears -- at once, so the value is computed where it is used. Same rule -- (PetActionBarFrame.lua:170-174): the two bars share this row, so a pet bar shown -- while the stance bar is up starts 20px past the last stance button. That case is -- rare but real — a possessed or charmed unit gives a pet bar to a class that also -- has forms. local bottomLeftUp = BenillaMultiBarBottomLeft and BenillaMultiBarBottomLeft:IsShown() if ( BenillaSlidingActionBarTexture0 and BenillaSlidingActionBarTexture1 ) then if ( bottomLeftUp ) then BenillaSlidingActionBarTexture0:Hide() BenillaSlidingActionBarTexture1:Hide() else BenillaSlidingActionBarTexture0:Show() BenillaSlidingActionBarTexture1:Show() end end if ( BenillaPetActionBarFrame ) then PETACTIONBAR_XPOS = 36 local forms = GetNumShapeshiftForms and GetNumShapeshiftForms() or 0 if ( forms > 0 and BenillaShapeshiftBarFrame and BenillaShapeshiftBarFrame:IsShown() ) then local last = getglobal("BenillaShapeshiftButton"..forms) local right = last and last:GetRight() if ( right ) then PETACTIONBAR_XPOS = right + 20 end end -- The ref guards this on IsShown() because a hidden bar of its is mid-slide and -- owns its own anchor; ours has no slide, so re-seating a hidden frame is a -- no-op and the guard would only add an ordering trap (OnShow fires the pass). BenillaPetActionBarFrame:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", "BenillaActionBar", "BOTTOMLEFT", PETACTIONBAR_XPOS, PETACTIONBAR_YPOS) end
-- The under-minimap right stack (ref l.1740-1770): anchorY walks down capture bars → -- quest timer → durability → quest watch, each shown frame pushing the next one down -- by its own height. benilla ships the quest-timer, durability and quest-watch arms -- (below); the capture bars above them don't exist yet, so anchorY starts at the ref's -- initial 0. The reference never leaves DurabilityFrame on its static XML anchor -- (whose +40 hangs the side glyphs off-screen — director-caught): every pass seats it -- at -CONTAINER_OFFSET_X, minus 20 more when a showSeparate glyph -- (shield/off-weapon/ranged) extends the art to the right — then drops the quest -- tracker to the running anchorY so the two never collide at the same corner. local anchorY = 0 -- ref l.1753-1757 verbatim (decision 1150). Seated whether shown or not — the ref -- SetPoints unconditionally and only the height accrual is gated — so the frame is -- already in place the frame it appears. Nil-guarded like every row here: the -- durability-only test harness ships no quest-timer frame. if ( QuestTimerFrame ) then QuestTimerFrame:SetPoint("TOPRIGHT", "MinimapCluster", "BOTTOMRIGHT", -CONTAINER_OFFSET_X, anchorY) if ( QuestTimerFrame:IsShown() ) then anchorY = anchorY - QuestTimerFrame:GetHeight() end end if ( DurabilityFrame ) then local durabilityOffset = 0 if ( DurabilityShield:IsShown() or DurabilityOffWeapon:IsShown() or DurabilityRanged:IsShown() ) then durabilityOffset = 20 end DurabilityFrame:SetPoint("TOPRIGHT", "MinimapCluster", "BOTTOMRIGHT", -CONTAINER_OFFSET_X-durabilityOffset, anchorY) if ( DurabilityFrame:IsShown() ) then anchorY = anchorY - DurabilityFrame:GetHeight() end end -- QuestWatchFrame is last in the ref's walk (l.1770), seated at the running anchorY so -- it drops below the durability guy when he shows instead of overlapping him (both -- anchor this same MinimapCluster corner — director-caught). benilla's tracker is -- BenillaQuestWatchFrame; nil-guarded because the durability-only test harness (and -- any config without a quest log) ships no such frame. if ( BenillaQuestWatchFrame ) then BenillaQuestWatchFrame:SetPoint("TOPRIGHT", "MinimapCluster", "BOTTOMRIGHT", -CONTAINER_OFFSET_X, anchorY) end end
-- ref UIParent.lua:1819-1878, transcribed 1:1 (decision 1008 — closes 0997's -- "abbreviates through KEY_ABBR" residue with the REAL mechanism: it never was a -- KEY_ABBR set; the whole abbreviation is this Lua). The action bar's HotKey corners -- call it with returnAbbr=1: ONE modifier abbreviates (CTRL→c, SHIFT→s, ALT→a — so -- SHIFT-2 reads "s-2", the director's ask), TWO OR MORE collapse the whole label to -- "·" — the ref's own multi-modifier dot. The full form (tooltips, the Keybindings -- page) keeps the canonical prefixes and reads the base key's KEY_* global. -- Transcription notes: the ref's dead `gsub(tempName, "CAPSLOCK", "Caps")` line -- (result discarded — gsub doesn't mutate) is dropped; its GetLocale() deDE -- CTRL→STRG swap and IsMacClient() KEY_*_MAC lookup ride behind existence guards -- (this VM defines neither yet, and the getglobal fallback covers the gap). function GetBindingText(name, prefix, returnAbbr) if ( not name ) then return ""; end local tempName = name; local i = strfind(name, "-"); local dashIndex = nil; local count = 0; while ( i ) do if ( not dashIndex ) then dashIndex = i; else dashIndex = dashIndex + i; end count = count + 1; tempName = strsub(tempName, i + 1); i = strfind(tempName, "-"); end
local modKeys = ''; if ( not dashIndex ) then dashIndex = 0; else modKeys = strsub(name, 1, dashIndex); if ( GetLocale and GetLocale() == "deDE" ) then modKeys = gsub(modKeys, "CTRL", "STRG"); end end
if ( returnAbbr ) then if ( count > 1 ) then return "·"; else modKeys = gsub(modKeys, "CTRL", "c"); modKeys = gsub(modKeys, "SHIFT", "s"); modKeys = gsub(modKeys, "ALT", "a"); modKeys = gsub(modKeys, "STRG", "st"); end end
if ( not prefix ) then prefix = ""; end local localizedName = nil; if ( IsMacClient and IsMacClient() ) then localizedName = getglobal(prefix..tempName.."_MAC"); end if ( not localizedName ) then localizedName = getglobal(prefix..tempName); end if ( not localizedName ) then localizedName = tempName; end return modKeys..localizedName; end
-- ref UIParent.lua:1051-1057, transcribed 1:1 (decision 1062). The reference's own -- list joiner, and it is exactly as plain as it looks: a bare ", " between every item, -- with NO "and" before the last one and NO localization string of any kind — 1.12 has -- no LIST_DELIMITER/AND global for it to reach for, and it does not build one. (The -- richer `BuildColoredListString` right below it in the reference — the per-item -- met/unmet red — already lives in TradeSkillFrame.xml as a guarded global, 0437 phase -- 3; folding that one up here beside this is a follow-up, not this slice's churn.) -- -- Callers: the pet paper doll's diet tooltip and PetStable.lua's, both as -- `format(PET_DIET_TEMPLATE, BuildListString(GetPetFoodTypes()))`. -- -- ZERO arguments returns NIL, not "" — the ref reads `arg[1]` off an empty vararg and -- returns it unchanged. That is load-bearing: `format("%s", nil)` errors, so a caller -- that can pass nothing (a warlock minion's empty diet) must be gated by its own UI, and -- it is — the diet icon is hunter-only. Quietly returning "" here would hide that. -- -- Lua-5.0 `arg`/`arg.n` has no equivalent (LUA_COMPAT_VARARG isn't shipped) — -- `select("#", ...)`/`select(i, ...)`, TradeSkillFrame.xml's own substitution. function BuildListString(...) local n = select("#", ...); if ( n == 0 ) then return nil; end local list = select(1, ...); for i = 2, n do local item = select(i, ...); list = list..", "..item; end return list; end
-- BenillaChatEdit_InsertLink(link) → true if it went in, else nil (decision 1059). -- -- Every shift-click site in this UI does the same two things before inserting: check the -- chat edit box is up, and — ours alone — check the link is not nil. That nil case is -- **benilla's, not the reference's**: our item templates resolve asynchronously -- (`CMSG_ITEM_QUERY_SINGLE`, answered a frame or many later), so a `Get…Link` getter -- legitimately answers nil for a slot whose name and quality have not landed, where the real -- client's synchronous item cache always has one. `EditBox:Insert` takes a string (the -- byte-modelled `0x77bee0`), so an unguarded nil is a script error — which is exactly the -- bug this function exists to make impossible to reintroduce at the next site. A dozen call -- sites were growing a dozen copies of the same two-line guard, and three of them shipped -- without it. -- -- The RETURN is what lets a caller fork on "did chat take it?" — a bag slot's shift-click -- posts the link when chat is open and opens the stack splitter when it is not (ref -- ContainerFrame.lua:567-577). Blizzard themselves eventually factored this exact helper out -- for this exact reason: 2.0's `ChatEdit_InsertLink(text)`, returning true/false, called from -- every one of these sites. 1.12 has no such function, so ours carries a benilla name rather -- than pretending to be reference API. function BenillaChatEdit_InsertLink(link) if not link then return nil end if not ChatFrameEditBox or not ChatFrameEditBox:IsVisible() then return nil end ChatFrameEditBox:Insert(link) return true end
